newsitem.title: GERMANY: No halt seen after German DAX soars 4.2 percent.
newsitem.headline: No halt seen after German DAX soars 4.2 percent.

text.p: Onward and upward, and faster than ever, was the forecast from German share traders on Wednesday after the German DAX index surged 4.2 percent -- its biggest daily gain this year.

Despite capacity problems triggered by huge trading volumes, which forced a trading systems shutdown during the day, the blue chip index surged ahead to end an extended bourse session up 175.67 points at 4,406.09 points.
In after-bourse dealings, the IBIS DAX was up 113.95 points at 4,411.59 points.
The dollar was the driving force behind the gains.
The U.S. currency was trading just below 1.83 marks in the afternoon, almost two pfennigs above its level during share trading hours in Germany on Tuesday.

Hopes for a continued rally were also fuelled by signals that the Dow Jones index is likely to also continue on the record trail. Comments from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan had supported the theory that there will not be a rate hike in the near-term, dealers said.
Analysts at Dresdner Bank AG predicted that the DAX would breach the 5,000 point level in the next two weeks, but predicted a level of 4,500 points by the end of the year.

Shares in Deutsche Bank AG rose as much as 11 percent in bourse trade, closing the session up 8.05 marks at 124.70 marks after the bank beat forecasts to post a 27.5 percent rise in net profit to 1.5 billion marks.
The entire banking sector was strongly in favour in the wake of the massive merger plans announced earlier this week between Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG.
The merger, which allows Vereinsbank to effectively dispose of a large holding in insurer Allianz AG without incurring capital gains tax, has boosted hopes of more consolidation.
Deutsche was trading at 126 marks in IBIS trade.
Vereinsbank was up 11.5 percent at 11.50 marks and Hypo-Bank was up 6.31 percent at 79.20 marks.
